Where it began

Jordan Cox was born in Margate on 21 October 2000 and joined the Kent academy when he was ten. He went to Wellesley House School and then Felsted School, and played his club cricket for Sandwich Town. In 2018 he was player of the tournament in the ECB Super-4s competition, and that year he signed his first professional contract with Kent.

He played for England Under-19s from early 2019, finished one youth series as their leading run scorer, and went to the Under-19 World Cup in South Africa in 2020.

The player

Cox announced himself in August 2020. Against Sussex at Canterbury he turned his first first-class hundred into an unbeaten 238, sharing a stand of 423 with Jack Leaning, a Kent record for any wicket. No player born in the 2000s had made a hundred in England before him. A year later he hit an unbeaten 58 off 28 balls as Kent won the T20 Blast final.

He moved to Essex in 2023 and made a hundred in only his second match for them, against his old county. In 2025 he hit 139 not out from 60 balls against Hampshire and was named the Professional Cricketers' Association's Men's Player of the Year. His Test debut came in June 2026 against New Zealand, batting at seven, and in August he made his first Test fifty against Pakistan. By November 2026 he had played four Tests and scored 254 runs at 42.33, with three fifties and a best of 73.

What made him special

He scored quickly and in every format, and he was an athlete in the field. In that 2021 final he palmed the ball back from beyond the boundary for Matt Milnes to complete the catch, and Lewis Gregory was on his way. In Tests he had held nine catches by November 2026, and made a stumping when given the gloves.

The one thing missing from his Test record at that point was a hundred, though three fifties in seven innings suggested he knew the way.

Away from the middle

He saw a good deal of the cricket world early on. He played grade cricket in Australia, joined the Hobart Hurricanes and later the Melbourne Renegades in the Big Bash, and played in franchise leagues in Pakistan, South Africa and Sri Lanka. In December 2025 the Royal Challengers Bengaluru signed him for the 2026 Indian Premier League. He made his England debuts in the shorter formats in 2024, against Australia and the West Indies.

And finally

A double hundred, a record stand and a first in English cricket, all at the age of 19. Most of us spend that age trying to work out the washing machine.
